Attaching our redlined MSA (AmberTech_MSA_redline.docx) — please see the sections we flagged under Section 3 (Use of Outputs) and Section 7 (Data & Training).

High level asks from our side:
- Explicit carveout preventing Redwood from allowing outputs to be productized by third parties (we want downstream productization controls and attribution limits).
- An explicit opt-out that prevents our customer content from being used to train or fine-tune models (PII and proprietary prompts).
- A short telemetry/evidence commitment so we can verify adherence (S3 or secure share, retention window).

Hi all,

Thanks, Logan and Sophie. I reviewed AmberTech's redlines and propose the following concise clause we can insert under a new Section 3.4 (Customer Output & Training):

"Customer Output Use; Training Opt-Out. Customer retains title to Customer Content and any Outputs generated from Customer Content. Redwood and its service providers shall not (a) incorporate Customer Content or Outputs into any models or datasets used for training, fine-tuning, or improving models; nor (b) enable third parties to productize, repackage, resell, or otherwise commercialize Outputs derived from Customer Content, except as expressly authorized in writing by Customer.

Redwood will provide Customer with evidence of compliance upon request consisting of access logs and a secure, time-limited S3 export of telemetry related to the relevant usage. Redwood reserves the right to deliver redacted logs where required for confidentiality, but will use reasonable efforts to preserve auditability.

This opt-out applies to hosted and Redwood-managed private deployments where Redwood directly processes Customer Content. For on-premise deployments fully operated by Customer, Redwood will not collect training data unless separately contracted."

Operational notes:
- The telemetry export will be scoped (timestamps, request ids, model variant) and we propose a standard retention window of 30 days by default; AmberTech can request extensions (we should confirm acceptable retention).
- If AmberTech requires longer retention or narrower redaction guarantees we’ll need SOC/compliance review — may affect costs.

I attached a text file with the clause (proposed_clause.txt) and a short change-log. If AmberTech agrees to the clause above with a retention window, Karthik can prepare the order form and procurement flow.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
